# A map of the viruses

> *Viruses are classified by genome and structure, but they are encountered by how they spread. A map that shows both connects the biology to the patient.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Describe a virus by genome type, envelope and route of spread; name the group chapter for a described virus |
| The map | An interactive table of virus groups by genome, envelope, route of spread and persistence, like *A map of the bacteria* |
| Why the groups are named as they are | Family names (herpesviruses) and route names (arboviruses) side by side |
| How the group chapters work | The same layout as the bacterial group chapters: the group in one sentence, sorting key, main viruses with profiles and a who, where, how table, contrast pairs, supporting viruses, later in the course |
| Scenario questions | Given a few traits, name the group |
